grammar_rules.summary: Use avant de + infinitif présent to express an action occurring before another.
grammar_rules.explanation: Avant de is always followed by the present infinitive, not past.
usage: To indicate an action that happens before another.
restrictions: avant de is always followed by the present infinitive, never the past infinitive
The infinitive must have the same subject as the main verb; a different subject requires avant que + subjunctive
conditions: Avant de introduces an action that happens before another action.
The infinitive that follows is the present infinitive, never the past infinitive.
exceptions: avant de is always followed by the present infinitive, never the past infinitive
The infinitive must have the same subject as the main verb; a different subject requires avant que + subjunctive
agreement_rules: The present infinitive is invariable and shows no person or number agreement.
avant de is invariable and precedes the infinitive without any agreement marking.
transformations: Avant de partir, ferme la porte.
Avant de manger, lave-toi les mains.
common_traps: Do not use past infinitive after avant de.
